answer.evidence: The tile is mostly one large sloped ramp plane (rows 0-63) with a chevron texture, seen from above. The columns at x=12, 24 and 35 show no front-edge line followed by a vertical face. Instead they show a continuous ramp surface with only 1-row texture lines. Rows 64-79 are flat ground of uniform lightness, not a vertical south face. The dark brown strips on the left and right edges (rows 5-63) are the receding cut walls of the cliff flanking the ramp. No south-facing vertical face of 3 or more rows is drawn, so the tile reads as a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate beats the references on visible tones per tile (10 against 3 for grass and 7 for paving), and its dark edge pixels are tinted brown (11% neutral), so the outline is dark material tone rather than a sticker line. The ramp face is only chevron stripes in about 3-4 tan/olive steps, with no per-pixel grain or peat speckle. The bottom landing is a large single flat tan block of roughly 35x12 source pixels. Near-flat coverage is 20%, against 0% for both references, which confirms the flat fills. The dark side walls are also mostly smooth. Beodeul ground tiles carry texture dots across the whole surface, and this piece looks flatter and simpler than that, so it fails.

answer.evidence: The main body is the ramp, a sloped plane drawn as a field of chevron-textured olive rows 0-63 (column x=24 stays at L about 119-141 with thin darker contour lines every few rows). A dark line at row 63 and the flat uniform ground color from row 64 down (L about 136) mark where the slope meets the floor. There is no vertical south face across the ramp; the only vertical faces are the dark cliff cut walls on the left (about 5-10 px wide, widening downward) and the right (a narrow brown strip). The ramp reads as an inclined top surface with flanking side walls, not as a standing block with a top and a front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts look fine on paper: 10 visible tones per tile against 3 for grass and 7 for paving, and only 11% neutral dark edge pixels. The side walls are a tinted dark brown, so the outline reads as material-toned rather than a black sticker line. By eye, though, the ramp body is built from about 4 tones (light, mid and dark chevron bands plus a dark brown wall), which is thinner than Beodeul's 5-6 steps per material. The chevrons are regular stripes with almost no speckle, grain or per-clump variation like the reference grass tufts or the individually shaded paving stones. The bottom landing is a large single tan block of about 40x15 source pixels with no grain at all. That accounts for the 20% near-flat coverage, where both references have 0%. A careful artist would see this flat landing and the stripe-only ramp as flatter than the references, so it fails.
